issues.title: Restricted secant inequality is overclaimed as convexity along every ray
issues.failure_explanation: The prose says that the surrogate is convex on the segment between any point and the common minimiser. Lemma 1 establishes a positive radial inner product, not monotonicity of the directional derivative along that segment. A change in loss ranking can make the derivative jump down while the radial inner product remains positive. Four losses w² and one loss 4h(w), with unit Huber h and k=2, give a downward derivative jump at w=2+√2.
issues.overall_effect: The radial-convexity interpretation is false. The formal restricted-secant statement of Lemma 1 and the unique-stationary-point result of Theorem 1 survive.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the convexity assertion by the actual restricted-secant implication: positive radial drift and increase of the surrogate away from the common minimiser, with one-sided derivatives at ranking ties. Retain Lemma 1 and Theorem 1.
issues.why_classification: This is a limited weakening of a coherent geometric guarantee, rather than a correction preserving radial convexity. The replacement is explicit and local, and no dependent formal result is lost; hence moderate rather than serious. The short edit alone does not make the loss immaterial.

issues.title: Lemma 3 turns two upper bounds on the outlier-gradient sum into a lower bound on SGD bias
issues.failure_explanation: Let S be the norm of the summed outlier gradients at the SGD stationary point. Stationarity and smoothness give S≤(1−ε)nL d_S, and the gradient cap gives S≤εnG. These do not imply εG≤(1−ε)L d_S. The final identification of S with the minimum of its two bounds is also unsupported. Opposing bounded outlier gradients can cancel exactly or nearly. The n=6,k=2 Huber example has d_S=0 and d_M=1/16, while the advertised factor is α=1/2. An open near-cancellation variant has d_S=1/400 and d_M=199/3200.
issues.overall_effect: Lemma 3 is false and its use does not establish Theorem 2. The dependent claim that MKL stationary points are necessarily closer than the SGD point is itself false, even inside the good-ordering ball. The introductory categorical assertion that outliers preclude an unbiased SGD stationary point has the same cancellation root.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace G in the lower bound by the actual net magnitude g_S=||mean_out ∇f_i(w_S)||, yielding εg_S≤(1−ε)Ld_S. A comparison with the MKL upper bound then contains G/g_S and requires quantitative non-cancellation plus αG/g_S<1; this is a substantive new restriction. Without it, withdraw the universal relative-superiority guarantee and retain only independently valid absolute bounds. Merely excluding d_S=0 is inadequate because the counterexample persists near cancellation.
issues.why_classification: The demonstrated family defeats the core relative guarantee, including nonzero SGD bias and arbitrarily small corruption. The established repair withdraws that guarantee on a natural family of models; no complete comparable repair under the original scope is established. This supports serious severity, without claiming that every substantially weakened theorem is impossible.

issues.title: Lemma 4 applies full-loss curvature to a clean-only gradient sum
issues.failure_explanation: The proof lower-bounds the clean-only weighted radial inner product using λ constructed for the frozen full loss. Outlier curvature can contribute to that λ, so it cannot automatically lower-bound the clean part. An admissible bounded-gradient example has full coefficient 37/72 but clean coefficient 35/72 at a nonzero good-ordering stationary point.
issues.overall_effect: The written lower-bound step is invalid, but the local distance bound and its use in Theorem 2 admit a short complete bypass. The preceding paragraph already limits the analysis to the good-ordering ball; a separate literal-global-scope allegation is not counted.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Freeze all probabilities at w_M and let F_p=Σ_i p_i(w_M)f_i. Use the strong-convexity modulus of this frozen full loss, uniformly lower-bounded by λ. Since ∇F_p(w_M)=0, strong monotonicity gives λ||w_M−w*||≤||∇F_p(w*)||≤GΣ_out p_i(w_M)=Gε^k in the stated local ball. This proves exactly the required local bound without a clean-only curvature claim.
issues.why_classification: A standard short strong-convexity argument preserves the same bound, assumptions, local scope and use. It neither resolves nor inherits the separate cancellation and k-dependence defects in Theorem 2.

issues.title: Theorem 3 omits the clean-sample noise variance from its residual
issues.failure_explanation: The main residual contains no positive clean-gradient variance term. With no outliers and w_t=w*, its displayed right side is zero even when individual clean gradients at w* are nonzero. For two losses (w−1)²/2 and two losses (w+1)²/2, η=1/10 gives actual next squared error 1/100 under any choice of sample, contradicting the zero bound. Appendix Theorem 4 includes the missing contribution.
issues.overall_effect: The noisy-case statement of Theorem 3 is false as printed. The independently stated Appendix Theorem 4 supplies a valid residual; the noiseless specialisation is unaffected by adding the missing term.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add +2η_t Σ_good p_i(w_t)||∇f_i(w*)||² to the main definition of R_t, retaining the existing nonnegative extra outlier-gradient term if desired. Since the main recurrence multiplies R_t by η_t, this contributes the required 2η_t² clean variance. The appendix argument then proves this corrected, possibly looser bound.
issues.why_classification: The old source already supplies the correction through the appendix residual and the routine one-step second-moment expansion. It preserves the intended noisy one-step residual bound with its additive variance term and entails no new proof architecture or change in the step-size order of that term. Several correct residual repairs exist, so this is a mathematical minor issue rather than a uniquely forced transcription typo.

issues.title: Ordered conditional upper bounds are promoted to an actual expected-distance comparison
issues.failure_explanation: The surrounding prose advertises smaller actual expected distance for MKL whenever the stated sufficient conditions hold. The formal corollary only compares upper bounds at the same current point; even a valid ordering of those bounds does not order the two actual errors. For the balanced four-quadratic model at w_t=−1 and η=1/5, the bounds favour MKL but its exact next expected squared distance is larger than SGD. The exact expected unsquared distances have the same reversed order.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised actual-performance guarantee is false independently of the residual-order defect. Correcting the formal residual comparison alone cannot establish this prose claim. It also cannot yield a trajectory or limiting-horizon comparison from a single-point bound.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Withdraw the actual-error superiority assertion. State only a conditional comparison of the displayed upper bounds in regimes where that comparison is valid, and explicitly distinguish it from ordering actual errors or trajectories. Preserving an actual-performance claim would require a separate valid comparison argument and appropriate assumptions; none is established here.
issues.why_classification: The supported local edit removes the advertised comparison of actual performance, which is the mathematical identity of this prose claim. A comparison of upper bounds is not a comparable actual-error guarantee, as the explicit witness shows. No complete lower-loss repair retaining actual superiority is established.

issues.title: Corollary 1 orders signed outlier residuals incorrectly
issues.failure_explanation: The step from the weighted outlier residual to uniform weights 1/n treats signed summands as though decreasing their coefficients always decreases the sum. The term f_i(w*)−f_i(w_t) can be negative. Moreover, when fewer than half the samples are clean, some outlier probabilities exceed 1/n. A balanced noiseless quadratic example isolates the sign failure even when every outlier is underweighted. It contradicts both the appendix residual comparison and the matching main-text claim after Eq. (14).
issues.overall_effect: The formal residual comparison in Corollary 1 is false under its stated good-ordering and noise premises, under either sampling convention. This is a failure with the same contraction coefficient on both sides, not the unequal-contraction objection.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Retain the signed outlier excess E_out=Σ_out(p_i−1/n)[η²||∇f_i(w_t)||²+2η(f_i(w*)−f_i(w_t))] in the residual difference, together with the clean and noise terms. Without a proved condition controlling this quantity, remove the unconditional residual-order conclusion. Merely correcting the sampling formula or assuming all outlier probabilities are smaller does not repair the signed comparison.
issues.why_classification: The counterexample defeats the central guarantee of the corollary. The established repair removes that unconditional comparison; a complete recognisably comparable replacement under the advertised corruption regime has not been established. This is major mathematical loss. Stronger structural assumptions are possible directions, not asserted complete moderate repairs.

issues.title: Corollary 1 substitutes without-replacement rank probabilities for the chosen with-replacement sampler
issues.failure_explanation: Equation (29) uses p_(i)=2(n−i)/[n(n−1)], the without-replacement min-2 probability. The earlier explicit convention selects sampling with replacement, whose probability is (2n−2i+1)/n². The proof carries the wrong coefficients into its clean contraction excess and noise comparison, so this is not just an unused incorrect display.
issues.overall_effect: The corollary proof does not use the probability law of the algorithm selected for the paper. Both laws still suffer the independent signed-residual failure, so this mismatch is not its explanation or repair.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use (2n−2i+1)/n² throughout. For |G|≤n/2 the smallest clean excess p_i−1/n is at least 1/n² instead of 1/[n(n−1)]. Accordingly use n, rather than n−1, in the sufficient scalar noise inequality. The stated first noise alternative already meets this conservative condition; the corrected second alternative in I009 also does. Keep the signed outlier excess until it is legitimately controlled, as required by I008.
issues.why_classification: This root has a short, explicit probability and coefficient correction for the intended algorithm. It preserves the form and order of the local noise estimates without new architecture. Independent false conclusions of the same corollary are assessed in their own roots, not used to inflate this sampling correction.
